comparisons.peer_topic: Nonperforming loan income recognition and balance inclusion
comparisons.peer_summary: Nonperforming loans are included in average loan balances, and income on these loans is generally recognized on a cost recovery basis.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the accounting treatment and inclusion criteria for nonperforming or non-accrual credit assets. Chase (C) specifically discloses the geographic composition of its 'Asia Consumer' non-accrual loan balances, detailing inclusions of Poland, Russia, and Bahrain. In contrast, Bank of America (BAC) describes the general policy for 'nonperforming loans,' stating that they are included in average loan balances and that income is recognized on a cost recovery basis. While C focuses on the specific portfolio constituents of the non-accrual balance, BAC focuses on the recognition methodology for income on such assets.
